result:
The change was already complete: the rule is in `plan.py`, the README is updated, and it's in your commit `b3ca87b`, so I didn't change any app code. All nine test suites pass on fresh copies, and your real database's fingerprint stayed the same during the runs. Two suites failed at first because of my test scripts, which I fixed: one had lost a helper file, and one assumed your data has a single account (it now has two).

**One gap remains:** a first week cut short by a mid-week start can't always meet the rule.
- **One run left:** that run is the whole week, so the long run is 100%. All three plans in your data start this way, on a Saturday with only the long run left that week.
- **Two runs left:** a tempo or interval run plus the long run can reach about 60%, such as 5 km and 7.5 km.

**What I checked**
- **864 plan combinations, old generator vs new:**
  - Outside those short first weeks, the long run never went above 52% of the week.
  - Dates, run types and long-run distances didn't change.
  - Plans that didn't need a raise came out identical.
  - Cutback and taper weeks are exactly 75% and 70% of the level reached.
- **Through the real app, on a copy of your data:** I regenerated all three of your plans there. Every week with more than one run stayed at 50% or under, and the summary page and calendar export still work.

**How much weeks grow** (total km per week)

| Plan | Peak week before | Peak week now |
|---|---|---|
| New runner, marathon, 16 weeks | 40 | 64 |
| New runner, half marathon, 12 weeks | 23.5 | 36 |
| New runner, 5K, 8 weeks | 13.5 | 16 |
| Has run before, 25 km a week, 10K | 40 | 40 (no raise needed) |

**Two effects you may want to look at**
- **Big jumps for new runners:** the new-runner marathon goes from 8 km to 64 km a week in 14 weeks, well beyond 10% growth. That follows your rule, but it's a big load for a beginner.
- **High longest run:** a runner doing 15 km a week who enters a 20 km longest run now starts at 36 km, up from 25.5 km. Their long run is capped at the half marathon's 18 km peak, and the total is still double that.

**To see it:** restart the app. Existing plans keep their current runs until you edit them, and editing replaces any changes you've made to those runs.

**Questions for you**
- Should a short first week be handled differently? I left it alone because you asked for everything else to stay the same. The alternative is to shorten the long run that week, or make a lone run an easy run, which would meet the rule but not start the plan from the runner's longest recent run.
